writeup.p: C0B carries an action enum (START_SNEAKING, STOP_SNEAKING, START_SPRINTING, STOP_SPRINTING, STOP_SLEEPING, RIDING_JUMP, OPEN_INVENTORY) plus an int aux value used only for RIDING_JUMP. The server's processEntityAction maps it directly onto the player entity state: setSneaking, setSprinting, wakeUpPlayer, horse jump. It is a pure state packet with no position, which makes it the perfect carrier for sprint/sneak manipulation that must not touch movement packets.

processEntityAction switches on the action ordinal and mutates the player entity. STOP_SLEEPING also resets hasMoved = false so the next C03 position is accepted (this is why WakeUp/phase tricks use it). RIDING_JUMP sets horse jump power from the aux int. OPEN_INVENTORY opens the horse GUI. The client sends C0B from EntityPlayerSP on key presses; sprint is normally also mirrored inside C03PacketPlayer's sprinting flag, which is where anti-cheats cross-check.

Sprint modules (Rise 5.99 Sprint) intercept and rewrite C0B to keep sprint always-on. Sneak modules (Rise 5.99 Sneak, Rise 6.2.4 NCPSneak) send START/STOP_SNEAKING on a timer to trick anti-cheat sneak checks. Scaffold (Rise 5.99, Tenacity, VulcanSprint mode) sneaks while placing on edges. WTap (Rise 5.99, Spicy) sends STOP_SPRINTING then START_SPRINTING around hits to reset the target's knockback velocity. Sigma KeepSprint cancels STOP_SPRINTING entirely so the player keeps sprint speed after attacking.

The packet is unvalidated beyond the enum, so clients can send START_SPRINTING while standing still or STOP_SNEAKING while never having sneaked. Anti-cheats therefore correlate C0B with C03's sprinting flag and with the movement deltas: sprint flag on but forward speed zero flags. WTap's stop-sprint-while-close is measured against hit timing. Sneak-spam (sending sneak every N ticks) is the classic NCP/Verus phase and safewalk enabler.

overview: The entity-state switchboard. Sprint modules rewrite it, sneak modules spam it, scaffold sneaks with it, WTap stutters it, and KeepSprint eats the STOP_SPRINTING. Every trick exploits the gap between the boolean state the server stores and the movement the client actually sends.
server_handling: processEntityAction mutates playerEntity state: setSneaking/setSprinting booleans, wakeUpPlayer (which clears hasMoved so the next position packet passes the movement check), horse jump power, horse GUI. No rate limiting; the aux int is ignored for all actions except RIDING_JUMP.
protocol_notes: Fields: VarInt entityId (client player), VarInt action ordinal, VarInt aux (0 for non-horse actions). Sent in PLAY state. Vanilla sends START_SPRINTING/STOP_SPRINTING from the sprint key handler and sneak actions from the sneak key; modules send it from motion/update events.
anticheat_landscape: NCP's sprint check compares C0B against C03's onGround/sprinting fields and movement speed. Verus detects sprint-stutter (WTap) by knockback timing. Sneak-abuse (sending sneak while moving fast) flags on Intave and newer NCP; Rise 6.2.4 NCPSneak and the scaffold sprint modes exist precisely to shape these patterns per AC.

modules.name: Sprint
modules.purpose: Force sprint state server-side regardless of direction keys, and cancel sprint-stopping packets.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 Sprint cancels C0B STOP_SPRINTING on the send event and re-sends START_SPRINTING when the player should sprint. The silent+multiDirection mode lets the player sprint in any direction, not just forward, by suppressing the vanilla sprint C0B and setting the entity sprint flag directly.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketSendEvent (cancel STOP_SPRINTING); PreMotionEvent for flag management.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Sprinting sideways without the forward key is the classic flag; NCP checks movement direction vs sprint state. The module is aimed at servers where the sprint check is weak or where the player holds W.
modules.variations: Only Rise 5.99 ships a dedicated Sprint module in the corpus; other clients fold sprint control into Speed/Fly modules.

modules.name: Sneak
modules.purpose: Send START/STOP_SNEAKING on a timer to exploit sneak-based anti-cheat logic or to safely place/phase.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 Sneak sends START_SNEAKING every N ticks and STOP_SNEAKING between, keeping the server-side sneak state toggling; the module has an auto mode that only sneaks when needed (e.g. near edges). Rise 6.2.4 NCPSneak sends a sneak cycle specifically tuned to NCP's sneak check to allow movement tricks without flagging.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Rapid sneak toggling is the classic NCP safewalk/phase enabler and is heavily flagged on modern ACs; NCPSneak in Rise 6.x shapes the toggle timing to the AC.
modules.variations: Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 NCPSneak.java implements the NCP-tuned cycle.

modules.name: WTap
modules.purpose: Reset the target's knockback by briefly stopping sprint right at the hit, then re-sprinting.
modules.how_it_works: On the attack, if the target is in range and the player was sprinting, send STOP_SPRINTING then START_SPRINTING in the same tick (or on consecutive ticks). The server stops applying sprint-knockback multiplier to the target for that hit. Rise 5.99 WTap sends both packets back-to-back via sendPacketWithoutEvent; Spicy Wtap uses sendQueue.addToSendQueue.
modules.vanilla_hook: AttackEvent or pre-motion check with a tick counter; PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: WTap is semi-legit: real players stutter sprint during combat. Verus and newer checks measure the stop-sprint duration; sending both packets in one tick is distinguishable from human input.
modules.variations: Spicy Wtap.java sends the same pair via the raw send queue; Sigma Killaura also touches C0B in its attack routine.

modules.name: KeepSprint
modules.purpose: Cancel STOP_SPRINTING so the player keeps sprint speed after landing a hit.
modules.how_it_works: Sigma KeepSprint hooks EventPacket on the receive/send path, and when a C0B with STOP_SPRINTING is seen it cancels the event, leaving the server-side sprint flag set. The result is that attacking no longer drops the player out of sprint.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Keeping sprint through a hit is exactly what legit 1.8 players do with the sprint key held, so this is low-risk; the flag appears only if the client also cancels the C03 sprinting-flag change.
modules.variations: No other client ships a dedicated KeepSprint in the corpus; other clients fold it into Sprint/WTap behavior.

modules.name: Scaffold (sneak/sprint control)
modules.purpose: Send C0B sneaking while placing on block edges and control sprint state around placements.
modules.how_it_works: Scaffold sneaks (START_SNEAKING) when the player is near an edge so the server slows the player and the placement lands, then stops sneaking mid-air. Rise 5.99 Scaffold toggles sneaking based on edge distance (lines ~414-421); Tenacity ScaffoldModule stops/starts sprinting around the placement (lines ~122-125); Rise 6.2.4 VulcanSprint is a scaffold sprint mode that sends START_SNEAKING on a tick cycle to fake the sneak while sprinting (lines ~28, 56).
modules.vanilla_hook: Scaffold's own pre-motion loop; PacketUtil.send for C0B.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Sneak-while-sprinting is impossible legitimately, so ACs correlate the C0B stream with C03 speed; each scaffold sprint/tower mode exists to pick timings that the target AC does not check.
modules.variations: Rise 6.2.4 also ships WatchdogJumpSprint; Rise 6.1.30 VulcanSprint; Tenacity ScaffoldModule toggles sprint around placements; Rise 5.99 and Sigma 4.11 Scaffold send sneak directly.

general_hooks: PacketSendEvent (Sprint, KeepSprint), PreMotionEvent (Sneak, Scaffold), attack events (WTap). Sigma uses EventPacket; Rise 6.x uses Listener<PacketSendEvent> and scaffold sub-modes.
client_variations: Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent to bypass its own event loop. Spicy pushes to sendQueue directly. Sigma hooks EventPacket with an isIncoming guard. Rise 6.x uses PacketUtil.send and EventLink listeners, and its PingSpoofComponent parks C0B in the blink class list.
